prompt: Write a README for `widget-cli` v2.4.0. It converts widget manifests (v2 JSON) to TOML, reads from stdin, writes to stdout, exits 2 on a schema violation and prints the failing JSON pointer to stderr. Install: `npm install -g widget-cli`. Requires Node 20+. Flags: `--strict` rejects unknown keys, `--pretty` aligns output tables. Keep it short.

Write a pull request description. In `src/upload/retry.ts`, the client retried non-idempotent PUTs after a 500, creating duplicate objects; a customer reported 1,840 duplicates over 3 days. The fix keys retries on an `Idempotency-Key` header derived from the object digest, so a replayed PUT resolves to the same object. Adds two tests in `test/retry.spec.ts`: one asserting a replayed 500 produces one object, one asserting a genuine second upload still creates two. Closes #412.

Write an ADR. We must pick a job queue for the notification service: sustained 200 jobs/sec, peaks near 900/sec, at-least-once delivery, jobs are idempotent, and we already run Postgres 16 and Redis 7. Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY drops payloads over 8000 bytes and has no consumer groups, so fan-out needs application-side coordination. Redis Streams gives consumer groups and XAUTOCLAIM for stuck entries, but our Redis has no persistence enabled today, so adopting it requires turning on AOF. We chose Redis Streams and will enable AOF with everysec fsync.

Write a release note for storage-sdk v3.2.0. Resume now survives network flaps: the retry queue persists to `~/.cache/storage-sdk/queue.db` and reloads on start, so an upload interrupted by a dropped connection continues instead of restarting. Breaking: `upload()` drops its third positional argument `timeoutMs`; pass `{timeoutMs}` in the options object instead. Node 18 support ends in this release; minimum is now Node 20.

Write a cold outreach email. Recipient: Dana Whitfield, staff platform engineer at Verrix, who published a post on 2026-07-14 titled 'Our CI got 40% slower and nobody noticed' describing how divergent Kubernetes manifests across their four environments caused hour-long debugging sessions. We make widget-cli, which converts widget manifests from v2 JSON to TOML and flags keys that differ across environments. Goal is a reply, not a booked demo.

Write landing page copy for widget-cli, aimed at platform engineers who know manifest sprawl hurts but have not gone looking for a tool. Verified facts you may use, and no others: it converts widget manifests (v2 JSON) to TOML; `--diff-envs` prints keys whose values differ across named environments; it runs in CI as a GitHub Action; it is free and open source under Apache-2.0; on the Verrix codebase it cut a manifest audit from 45 minutes to under 30 seconds across 1,200 manifests.

Write a 3-post X thread about manifest sprawl in build pipelines. Verified facts you may use, and no others: divergent manifests across environments are a common cause of 'works in staging' failures; widget-cli's `--diff-envs` prints keys whose values differ across environments; it is free and Apache-2.0 licensed; it cut one team's manifest audit from 45 minutes to under 30 seconds across 1,200 manifests.
